atoms.text:
Remember Clara and Leonardo?
Now, Leonardo is visiting Clara in her home town Lisbon, Portugal. Leonardo is a handyman and loves tiles. Select the tile that says Lisbon to hear what Leonardo has to say.
atoms.sound: ssml: Remember Clara and Leonardo?<break time='600ms'/> Now, Leonardo is visiting Clara in her hometown Lisbon, Portugal. Leonardo is a handyman and loves tiles. Select the tile that says Lisbon to hear what Leonardo has to say.

atoms.text: For over 6,000 years, humans have used tiles to build houses or floors. Usually, the main ingredients for tiles are clay, sand and water. Today, tiles are made in huge factories, but the process has barely changed. In order to make tiles, you first have to mix those ingredients together.
atoms.sound: For over 6,000 years, humans have used tiles to build houses or floors. Usually, the main ingredients for tiles are clay, sand and water. Today, tiles are made in huge factories but the process has barely changed. In order to make tiles, you first have to mix those ingredients together.

atoms.text: In the next step, the mixture is pressed into a rectangular shape. After that, the tile has to dry. This drying process makes the tile solid and gives it more strength. In the final step, the tile is heated up in a very hot oven, up to 1,185°C. Then the tile only needs to cool down before it can be used.

instruction.text: Listen to the dialogue and answer the questions.

atoms.b: There are many buildings with tiles in Portugal, aren’t there?
atoms.sound: ssml: There are many buildings with tiles in Portugal, aren’t there? <break time='1500ms'/>

atoms.b: Yes, you are right. Tiles and Portugal have a long history. In Portugal, you will find tiles not only inside but also on the outside of buildings. Most of the tiles you see are blue and white. They either show a beautiful pattern or a fascinating picture.

instruction.text: True or false? Select the correct answer by combining the information you’ve learnt from both texts.

atoms.a: Although tiles have been used for over 6,000 years, the way they are produced has barely changed.
Tiles can be used inside and outside of buildings.
In winter, it is very cold in Portugal and tiles help to keep the inside warm.
Tiles come in many colours and shapes. They can even show a huge picture which tells a story of the past.
